clue.text: Worthless song-writer goes to New York

parts.note: a catch is a round for several voices, an old kind of song
a pen is the instrument that writes

explanation.surface: A second-rate lyricist leaves for New York to try his luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song-writer' reads as one person but splits into two pieces, a song and a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchpenny goods are cheap and showy, made only to tempt buyers, hence of little real value.

clue.text: A point is made by an Egyptian god

parts.note: the nub is the central point of a matter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity makes a telling point in a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Anubis is the jackal-headed deity of ancient Egypt who guided the dead.

clue.text: Pampering with a little fish, say?

indicators.note: say tells the solver the word for the fish is spoken and its sound kept

parts.note: a codling is a young cod, a small fish

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a pet with a treat of a little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Coddling means indulging or overprotecting someone, treating them too gently.

clue.text: Dictatorial peer replaced — politician, party man

indicators.note: replaced means put in another order, so the letters of peer are moved around

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A bossy lord is ousted by a politician who is a party loyalist.
explanation.walkthrough: PEER rearranged gives PERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peremptory means commanding in a way that permits no refusal or argument, hence domineering.

clue.text: Education of railwaymen — true, if misguided

parts.note: NUR is the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so the letters of true go out of order

explanation.surface: The training of railway workers is described as accurate but wrongly directed.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE rearranged gives TURE. The held text dropped the word 'true'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurture is the upbringing and training of a child, which is its rearing and schooling.

clue.text: Student, means to overturn the, boat

indicators.note: overturning turns a word upside down, which in a down entry reads it from the bottom

parts.note: a way is a means of doing something
L is the learner driver's plate, so it stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student is looking for a way to capsize the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To overturn' turns only the word for means; the student's L is then added at the end, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: After which the girl won't be missed'?

definitions.text: After which the girl won't be missed'?

parts.words: After which the girl won't be missed'
parts.note: looks like someone departing, but missed means addressed as Miss: after the wedding she becomes Mrs

explanation.surface: Something happens after which nobody will pine for a certain girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding changes a woman's title from Miss to Mrs.

clue.text: Room can do for wine

parts.note: a chamber is a room
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A cellar or a canister can serve as a store for wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambertin is a celebrated red Burgundy from Gevrey-Chambertin.

clue.text: A jolly peculiar hag-but county!

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters of the word hag are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that a strange old woman turns out to be a whole county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an intensifier ('jolly peculiar') but is a Royal Marine. ARMAGH is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagh is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Perhaps a striker made one late?

definitions.text: Perhaps a striker made one late?

parts.words: Perhaps a striker made one late
parts.note: a striker suggests a footballer or someone on strike, but here it is someone who strikes a fatal blow, making a victim 'the late' so-and-so

explanation.surface: A footballer or picketer made someone miss an appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer turns a living person into the late person, someone dead, by striking them.

clue.text: Message " reads — " get Mr Lea replaced"

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a new order, so the letters of get Mr Lea are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note reads that a Mr Lea should be swapped for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words look like the message's content; they are the anagram fodder, rearranged as signalled by 'replaced'.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by wire and delivered printed on paper.

clue.text: Like to take back vermouth and get wine?

parts.note: like and as are both used for comparing things

indicators.note: taking back means reading the word for vermouth from end to start

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in a gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether returning a vermouth will get them some wine instead.
explanation.walkthrough: IT, short for Italian vermouth, is read backwards to give TI. ASTI is a sparkling Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Diplomat, rising scholar and others repairing roads

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar
the other scholars are BAs, Bachelors of Arts

indicators.note: repairing means fixing or reworking, so the letters of roads are rearranged

explanation.surface: An envoy, a rising academic and others are mending the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: MA read upwards gives AM; 'others' continues the scholars as BAS; ROADS rearranged gives SADOR. Old-style, loose wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a senior envoy representing his country abroad.

clue.text: Little money comes in by time rate is given

indicators.note: comes in says the coin is put inside the other two pieces joined together

parts.note: per means by, as in miles per hour
an age is a long period of time
a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: A small sum of money arrives as time goes by and a rate is set.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a rate or proportion expressed out of a hundred.

clue.text: Backing horses by mathematical formula? That's about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the formula is placed round the word it

parts.note: an equation is a mathematical statement of equality, a formula
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bets on racehorses using a mathematical system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing horses' suggests betting, but means getting on their backs, riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitation is the art of horse riding, sitting on a mount's back.

clue.text: Grow food in retirement-a change for one

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word for food is read backwards

parts.note: grub is informal for food

indicators.note: a change for means the letters of one are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes up gardening in retirement, a welcome change.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUB read backwards gives BURG, and ONE rearranged gives EON.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to begin to grow or put out shoots, so it means to flourish or expand.

clue.text: Food for a beery sort, in a way

indicators.note: in tells us the shuffled letters go inside the way

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters of a beery are put in order anew

explanation.surface: Something to eat for a beery type, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' rearranges the letters of 'a beery', and 'in' sets that mix inside the abbreviation for road.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye bread is a loaf made with rye flour.

clue.text: Barker let parts of stream

parts.note: a cur is a dog, an animal that barks
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A dog lets parts of a stream go by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' sounds like a man's name or a fairground caller but is just a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A current is a flowing body of water, the moving part of a river or stream.

clue.text: Economize concerning rent distributed to church

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of rent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parish cuts costs by passing rent on to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: RENT rearranged gives TREN.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut back spending, to be thrifty.

clue.text: Malicious gossip in note held by sole supporter

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so the note goes within the footwear

parts.note: a sandal supports the sole of the foot
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Gossip about a musical note kept up by a lone patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole supporter' looks like an only backer but is footwear under the sole.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is outrage-provoking talk that damages reputations.

clue.text: Seth may act as replacement in this craft

indicators.note: as replacement says the letters of Seth may act are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: An understudy named Seth may take over a part on board this vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam yacht is a pleasure vessel driven by a steam engine, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Rent collector never content?

indicators.note: the content of something is what it holds, so the letters are found held within the words collector never

explanation.surface: A rent collector is never satisfied with what he takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord but is the past participle of rend. The run sits across collecTOR Never. The '7' in the held text is an OCR slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the past participle of rend, meaning ripped apart, so it is a synonym for ripped.

clue.text: Brook's written to hurry up Len

explanation.definitionFit: A runnel is a small stream or rivulet.

clue.text: Article" about' Greek, song concerning land"'

explanation.surface: A newspaper article discusses a Greek folk song about the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a piece of journalism but is the grammatical indefinite article, which 'about' puts round the Greek song.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian means relating to farmland and its cultivation.

clue.text: 'Ow this bit of news will strike people?

explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single piece of news in a paper or bulletin.

clue.text: Condescending of Parisian to take two gin cocktails

indicators.note: cocktails are mixed drinks, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Parisian deigns to accept two gin cocktails.

explanation.definitionFit: Deigning means stooping to do something beneath one's dignity, which is acting condescendingly.
